newsitem.title: USA: U.S. productivity up 0.6 percent in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. productivity up 0.6 percent in second quarter.

text.p: Productivity gains at American businesses outside the agricultural sector slowed in the second quarter and were slower in the first quarter than previously estimated, the Labor Department said on Tuesday.

Non-farm productivity rose at a 0.6 percent seasonally adjusted annual rate between April and June, down from a 1.4 percent growth rate in the first three months of the year, the department said. It previously had estimated that first-quarter productivity rose at a 2.6 percent pace.
Wall Street economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 0.7 percent gain in second-quarter productivity and a 2.7 percent jump in unit labour costs.
Unit labour costs, which figure heavily in the prices of goods and services, rose at a 2.4 percent pace in the second quarter after a 3.1 percent gain in the first quarter, the department said.

Productivity, a measure of business efficiency that is based on output of goods and services per worker hour, rose 1.3 percent in 1996 after a meagre 0.2 percent gain in 1995. Unit labour costs rose 1.8 percent last year and 2.4 percent in 1995.

Federal Reserve policy-makers, who will meet next week to decide whether to raise interest rates, have been closely watching productivity reports, although many economists believe that they have been understating actual productivity gains as the U.S. economy has become more service-oriented. Productivity gains allow increases in worker pay and benefits to be absorbed by employers without forcing price hikes or eating into profits.
